subtitle: How Jajau Lit the Last Century of the Mughals

panels.shot: epic split-panel composition, half showing Muazzam/Bahadur Shah I in armor, half Azam Shah on an elephant, with a hazy battlefield of tents and guns behind them
panels.action: Bahadur Shah I & Azam Shah stand back to back, each facing a different horizon of dusty plains and massed Mughal ranks, storm clouds rolling over the camp at Jajau between Agra and Dholpur.

dialogue.text: In June 1707, on the parched ground of Jajau, Aurangzeb’s own sons turned their guns on each other—and the first crown after him was hammered out of that single day of fire.

i18n.hi: जून 1707, जाजऊ की सूखी ज़मीन पर, औरंगज़ेब के बेटों ने ही एक–दूसरे पर तोपें तान दीं — और उसी आग के एक दिन में उसके बाद का पहला ताज गढ़ा गया।

panels.shot: wide aerial view over Aurangabad, fading into a stark deathbed interior
panels.action: A dim chamber in Aurangabad shows Aurangzeb’s frail form on a low bed, scribes and princes’ envoys waiting outside as the Deccan plains stretch away under a hot, fading sun.

dialogue.text: Aurangzeb died far from Delhi, at Aurangabad, in February 1707. His empire stretched from Kabul to the Cauvery, but he left no clear, binding order for who would rule it next.

i18n.hi: फरवरी 1707 में औरंगज़ेब दिल्ली से दूर औरंगाबाद में मरा। साम्राज्य काबुल से कावेरी तक फैला था, पर उसने अगला बादशाह तय करने का कोई पक्का हुक्म नहीं छोड़ा।

panels.shot: tight interior split, showing two separate tents, each with a prince hearing the news
panels.action: In one Deccan camp, Azam Shah grips a letter with tense pride; in another, Muazzam sits in a northern pavilion, brows furrowed, as a messenger whispers the news of their father’s death.

dialogue.text: Muazzam, the elder surviving son in the north, and Azam Shah, the younger near Aurangzeb’s bier, each heard the news and each saw, in that silence, a throne.

i18n.hi: उत्तरी सूबे में बड़े ज़िंदा बेटे मुअज़्ज़म और जनाज़े के पास बैठे छोटे बेटे आज़म शाह — दोनों ने खबर सुनी, और खामोशी में दोनों ने ही एक तख़्त देखा।

panels.shot: low-angle view of Azam in the Deccan proclaiming himself emperor before a gathered court
panels.action: Azam Shah stands under a canopy in the Deccan, sword raised, courtiers bowing as a makeshift throne is set behind him and elephants trumpeting faintly in the camp beyond.

dialogue.text: Azam acted first. Near the corpse of the old emperor, he took the title of Shah Alam, drew Deccan officers to his side, and marched north, convinced speed would crown him.

i18n.hi: आज़म ने पहले वार किया। बूढ़े बादशाह की लाश के पास ही उसने ‘शाह आलम’ की पदवी ली, दक्कनी अमीरों को साथ बुलाया और यक़ीन के साथ उत्तर की ओर चला कि रफ़्तार ही उसे ताज दिलाएगी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Muazzam in prayerful posture, then leaning over a map with Rajput and Afghan captains
panels.action: Muazzam kneels on a mat in quiet prayer inside a tent, then rises to confer over a spread map with Rajput chiefs and Afghan commanders, their fingers tracing the road to Agra.

dialogue.text: Muazzam waited, hesitated, then moved. He had once rebelled and been chained by his father, and knew caution, but he also knew that whoever reached Agra and its treasure first would speak as emperor.

i18n.hi: मुअज़्ज़म पहले रुका, डगमगाया, फिर चला। कभी बग़ावत कर के बाप से ज़ंजीरें खा चुका था, एहतियात जानता था, पर यह भी समझता था कि जो पहले आगरा और उसके ख़ज़ाने पर बैठेगा, वही बादशाह बोलेगा।

panels.shot: broad landscape of north India, arrows on a ghostly map overlay showing both princes racing toward Agra
panels.action: The dusty roads of the north show caravans of war—Azam’s columns pushing up from the south-west, Muazzam’s forces rolling down from the north—while a faint, translucent map hovers, lines converging near Agra.

dialogue.text: Both princes aimed at Agra. Its fort, its mint, and the imperial harem meant legitimacy. Their letters spoke of obedience and duty, but their drums spoke of war.

i18n.hi: दोनों की नज़र आगरा पर थी। क़िला, टकसाल और शाही हरम ही असली वैधता थे। ख़तों में फ़रमाबरदारी और फ़र्ज़ की बातें थीं, पर ढोल सिर्फ़ जंग की जुबान बोल रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot on Muazzam’s mixed army, highlighting diversity—Mughal cavalry, Rajput horsemen, Afghan warriors, and a small Sikh contingent in the distance
panels.action: Muazzam rides along a long, uneven line of horse and foot—Mughal troopers in quilted armor, Rajput nobles with plumed turbans, Afghan riders with tall caps, and, at a distance, a small group of turbaned Sikh warriors.

dialogue.text: Muazzam’s strength lay in alliances. Khafi Khan notes the Mughal, Afghan and Rajput chiefs who backed him; later Sikh chronicles remember a small band of Guru Gobind Singh’s Sikhs marching in wary support.

i18n.hi: मुअज़्ज़म की ताक़त थे उसके गठजोड़। ख़ाफ़ी ख़ाँ ने उसके साथ खड़े मुग़ल, अफ़ग़ान और राजपूत सरदारों के नाम दर्ज किए; सिख इतिहास आगे चलकर गुरु गोबिंद सिंह के थोड़े से सतर्क सिखों को भी उसके हक़ में चलते याद रखते हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle on Azam’s war council at a riverside camp, artillery in the background
panels.action: Azam Shah stands beside a riverbank camp near Dholpur, guns lined up behind him, as he confers with seasoned Deccan officers, their faces lined from long wars in the south.

dialogue.text: Azam brought with him hardened Deccan troops and gunners who had fought the Marathas for years. Kamwar Khan describes his confidence; he believed experience and nearness to the corpse gave him right and strength.

i18n.hi: आज़म अपने साथ दक्खन के घिसे–पिटे सिपाही और तोपची लाया, जो बरसों मराठों से भिड़े थे। कमवार ख़ाँ उसकी ठसक लिखता है; उसे यक़ीन था कि अनुभव और मय्यत के क़रीब होना ही उसका हक़ और बल है।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Jajau plain at dawn, both camps faintly visible on opposite banks of the Chambal
panels.action: The sun rises over the flat, scrubby plain of Jajau near the Chambal, tents and lines of pickets stretching on both sides of the river, war elephants dim shapes in the morning haze.

dialogue.text: By June they faced each other near Jajau, between Agra and Dholpur. Chroniclers differ over exact numbers, but they agree on this: two royal camps, one narrow plain, and no room for retreat.

i18n.hi: जून तक वे आगरा और धौलपुर के बीच, जाजऊ के पास आमने–सामने आ खड़े हुए। तारीख़नवीस गिनतियों पर लड़ते हैं, पर इस पर सहमत हैं: दो शाही डेरे, एक तंग मैदान, और पीछे हटने की कोई गुंजाइश नहीं।

panels.shot: close-up on Muazzam’s face inside his tent at night, lit by a small lamp, with a sealed paper bearing Aurangzeb’s hand beside him
panels.action: In the dim lamplight of a tent, Muazzam’s lined face is caught between worry and resolve, his hand resting near an old letter in Aurangzeb’s handwriting, its seal cracked long ago.

dialogue.text: Stories spread that Aurangzeb had once toyed with dividing the empire among his sons. But by Jajau those speculations meant little. As Muazzam knew, in the Mughal house the field, not papers, decided succession.

i18n.hi: किस्से फैले थे कि औरंगज़ेब कभी साम्राज्य बेटों में बाँटने की बात सोचता था। पर जाजऊ तक आते–आते ये कयास बेमानी थे। मुअज़्ज़म जानता था, मुग़ल ख़ानदान में तख़्त कागज़ नहीं, मैदान तय करता है।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot as both armies deploy, dust clouds rising, artillery being positioned
panels.action: Both armies pour out of their camps, cannons dragged into place, cavalry squadrons wheeling, and elephants lumbering into the center, dust and heat shimmering across the Jajau plain.

dialogue.text: At dawn on 20 June 1707, they formed for battle. Artillery in the center, cavalry on the wings, elephant corps in front—a familiar Mughal pattern, but this time the foe was family.

i18n.hi: 20 जून 1707 की सुबह वे जंग के लिए क़तार में खड़े हुए। बीच में तोपें, पंखों पर सवार, आगे हाथियों की पंक्ति — वही पुराना मुग़ल नक़्शा, बस इस बार दुश्मन ख़ानदान का था।

panels.shot: medium shot focusing on Azam Shah atop a richly caparisoned elephant, pointing his sword toward Muazzam’s lines
panels.action: Azam Shah rides high on a decorated war elephant, his armor gleaming, as he points his sword toward the distant lines of Muazzam’s army, his son beside him on another elephant.

dialogue.speaker: bahadur_shah_i_and_azam_shah
dialogue.text: “Today, brother, the empire itself shall know its master.”

i18n.hi: "आज, भाई, ख़ुद साम्राज्य अपने मालिक को पहचानेगा।"

panels.shot: medium shot on Muazzam on horseback, surrounded by mixed contingents, a Rajput chief at his side
panels.action: Muazzam sits firm on a sturdy horse, flanked by a Rajput noble in jeweled mail and an Afghan commander, their lances pointing forward as their combined line begins to advance.

dialogue.speaker: bahadur_shah_i_and_azam_shah
dialogue.text: “Hold your ground. Let their pride break on our guns.”

i18n.hi: "ज़मीन पकड़े रहो। उनकी झूठी शान हमारी तोपों पर टूटने दो।"

panels.shot: chaotic battlefield wide shot, cannon smoke, cavalry charges, elephants pushing through, but no gore
panels.action: The field at Jajau is a haze of smoke and dust as cannons flare, cavalry charge and wheel, elephants push forward through broken lines, and banners of both brothers tilt and sway above the confusion.

dialogue.text: Khafi Khan and Kamwar Khan describe a hard, shifting fight. Artillery tore lanes; some wings held, others sagged. Allies watched which way the wind of fortune began to blow.

i18n.hi: ख़ाफ़ी ख़ाँ और कमवार ख़ाँ एक सख़्त, बदलती जंग का ज़िक्र करते हैं। तोपों ने रास्ते चीर दिए; कुछ पाँखें टिक गईं, कुछ ढह गईं। हमसफ़र देखते रहे कि नसीब की हवा किस तरफ़ चलती है।

panels.shot: focused shot near Azam’s elephant as its mahout falters and the beast turns, sowing confusion among his guards
panels.action: Near the center, Azam’s elephant lurches and turns amid the press, its mahout slumped and guards in sudden disarray, as enemy fire flashes in the distance.

dialogue.text: In the thick of the struggle, Azam’s center faltered. Chroniclers note confusion around his elephant; whether from a wounded driver or broken ranks, order slipped, and with it, the heart of his army.

i18n.hi: ठनाई के बीच आज़म का बीचला हिस्सा डगमगा गया। तारीख़नवीस उसके हाथी के आसपास घपले का ज़िक्र करते हैं; कहीं महावत के ज़ख़्मी होने से, कहीं क़तारें टूटने से, क़ायदा फिसला और साथ ही उसकी फ़ौज का दिल बैठ गया।

panels.shot: intense medium shot of Azam and his son still fighting atop their elephants amidst retreating soldiers
panels.action: Azam Shah and his son stand tall on their elephants, still urging on a dwindling guard, while around them some of their own cavalry begin to peel away from the field.

dialogue.text: Azam and his son did not withdraw. The Persian accounts agree on this: they fought on as men around them broke, holding to the old Mughal code that a prince should not turn his back.

i18n.hi: आज़म और उसका बेटा पीछे नहीं मुड़े। फ़ारसी बयानात इस पर एक हैं: साथ वाले टूटते रहे, पर वे पुराने मुग़ल उसूल पर डटे रहे कि शाहज़ादा पीठ नहीं दिखाता।

panels.shot: somber mid-distance shot showing Azam’s fallen elephant in the aftermath, with Muazzam’s troops cautiously approaching
panels.action: In the quiet after the clash, an elephant lies still on the trampled ground, Azam Shah’s lifeless form slumped on the howdah, as Muazzam’s armored troopers approach with wary, measured steps.

dialogue.text: By evening, Azam Shah and his sons lay dead near Jajau. With them fell their claim. The chroniclers are clear: the line that had marched from Aurangzeb’s deathbed was cut off in a single day.

i18n.hi: शाम तक आज़म शाह और उसके बेटे जाजऊ के पास खेत रहे। उनके साथ उनकी दावेदारी भी मिट गई। तारीख़नवीस साफ लिखते हैं: औरंगज़ेब की मौत के बिस्तर से चली वह शाख़ एक ही दिन में काट दी गई।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot of Muazzam entering Agra Fort in state, but with wary eyes and heavily armed guards
panels.action: Muazzam rides in formal procession through the great gate of Agra Fort, drums and trumpets ahead, but his face remains guarded and lines of musketeers watch from the walls.

dialogue.text: From Jajau, Muazzam moved to Agra and the imperial ladies. Taking control of the fort and treasury, he assumed the title Bahadur Shah I—victor by battle, emperor in name.

i18n.hi: जाजऊ से मुअज़्ज़म सीधा आगरा गया और शाही ख़वातीन तक पहुँचा। क़िले और ख़ज़ाने पर क़ब्ज़ा कर उसने बहादुर शाह पहले का ख़िताब लिया — जंग से फ़तहयाब, नाम से बादशाह।

panels.shot: closer shot of Bahadur Shah I on the Peacock Throne, the hall grand yet shadowed, courtiers divided into cautious clusters
panels.action: Bahadur Shah I sits on the Peacock Throne in the Diwan-i-Khas, courtiers in rich robes assembled below, some faces relieved, others calculating, as shafts of light cut through the high hall.

dialogue.text: Yet the victory was narrow and the loyalties that made it so were fragile. Irvine and Richards note how each commander watched for reward, and how every province now knew that a prince could fall to his brother.

i18n.hi: पर जीत तंग थी और जिसने उसे मुमकिन बनाया, वे वफ़ादारियाँ नाज़ुक थीं। आयरविन और रिचर्ड्स लिखते हैं कैसे हर सरदार इनाम की राह देख रहा था, और हर सूबे को अब पता था कि शाहज़ादा भाई के हाथ भी गिर सकता है।

panels.shot: wide temporal montage: Jajau’s battlefield fading into later scenes of rebellion and faction around the Mughal court
panels.action: The trampled plain of Jajau dissolves into later images—a court beset by quarrelling nobles, distant governors in their own palaces, and the imperial standard flying over a shrinking realm.

dialogue.text: Jajau opened the last century of the Mughals. A crown won against a brother carried the crack of that first shot within it, and every later struggle in Delhi echoed the day when Aurangzeb’s sons met by the Chambal.

i18n.hi: जाजऊ ने मुग़लों की आख़िरी सदी का दरवाज़ा खोला। जो ताज भाई के ख़ून से जीता गया, उसमें उस पहली गोली की दरार बस गई, और दिल्ली की हर बाद की कश्मकश में चंबल किनारे औरंगज़ेब के बेटों की वह मुलाक़ात गूँजती रही।
